reasoning: L1 cited Paladin alongside Boss Energy as examples of uranium mine restarts proving more challenging than anticipated, with both companies having downgraded their restart expectations. This was used to illustrate the broader point that supply-side response to higher uranium prices is slower and harder than the market might assume, supporting the structural deficit thesis.
quote: While improved uranium prices have started to incentivise mine restarts and to re-engage enthusiasm for new projects, restarts have proven more challenging (e.g. Paladin and Boss have both downgraded expectations on restarts) and there are only a handful of significant projects that are well enough progressed through feasibility and permitting that could come into production over the next five years.
episode_title: 2025 Sep L1 Long Short Fund Ltd Quarterly Report

headline: Blackwattle reduces Paladin Energy position after flood disruption delays Langer Heinrich ramp-up and soft uranium spot price weigh on outlook.
reasoning: Paladin's Langer Heinrich mine was hit by a 1-in-50 year flood event in March, causing the stock to drop 25.7%. While production is only impacted for a small number of weeks, the delays have pushed out the timeline to reach nameplate capacity, a key milestone. This ramp-up delay, combined with continued softness in the uranium spot price and general equity market uncertainty, has kept pressure on the share price. Blackwattle has reduced the size of the position and is awaiting further clarity from management on the ramp-up timeline, expected to be provided on the March quarterly investor call.
quote: Paladin Energy dropped 25.7% in March, driven by the disruption from a '1-in-50 year' flood event to its Langer Heinrich mine. The company has since provided more clarity on the extent of damage, and while production will only be impacted for a small number of weeks, the delays have pushed out the timeline to reach nameplate capacity, which remains a key milestone. This ramp-up delay combined with continued softness in the spot price and general equity market uncertainty has seen Paladin's share price continue to fall. As such we have reduced the size of the position and await more clarity from management regarding the timing of the Langer Heinrich ramp-up.
episode_title: Blackwattle Small Cap Long Short Quality Fund Monthly March 2025

headline: Blackwattle holds Paladin Energy as key uranium exposure, seeing material share price outperformance potential as Langer Heinrich mine approaches full production
reasoning: Paladin Energy is the fund's key exposure to the nuclear demand thematic and the need for baseload power to support growing intermittent renewable generators. As a uranium producer rather than a developer, Paladin is well-positioned to benefit from the near-term supply shortfall and high incentive pricing required to stimulate further uranium production. The December quarterly highlighted progress in resolving previously disclosed ramp-up issues at the Langer Heinrich mine. PDN shares experienced a significant sell-off in late 2024, but with full production expected over the next six months, the managers see potential for material share price outperformance.
quote: Paladin Energy is the fund's key exposure to the nuclear demand thematic and the need for baseload power to support the growing fleet of intermittent renewable generators. As a uranium producer (not a developer), Paladin is well-positioned to benefit from the near-term supply shortfall and the high incentive pricing required to stimulate further uranium production. In January, PDN shares rose 10% following the release of its December quarterly update, which highlighted progress in resolving previously disclosed ramp-up issues at the Langer Heinrich mine. While such challenges are common during ramp-up phases, PDN shares experienced a significant sell-off in late 2024. With the company expected to reach full production over the next six months, we see potential for material share price outperformance.
episode_title: Blackwattle Small Cap Long Short Quality Fund Monthly January 2025

headline: Salt holds Paladin Energy as a lower-risk uranium play amid a highly positive price outlook and major future supply deficit
reasoning: Paladin rose +15.0% in August and has been a solid performer for the fund in recent months. The uranium price outlook is extremely positive as numerous countries look to add nuclear capacity to lower carbon emissions. A major future supply deficit is expected to be exacerbated by the Russian situation. Salt chose PDN over smaller, higher-risk sector peers because of its relatively lower risk profile and the restart of the Langer Heinrich mine in Namibia.
quote: The second key tailwind came from a mid-sized holding in Paladin Energy (PDN, +15.0%), which has been a solid performer for the Fund in recent months. The uranium price outlook appears extremely positive, with numerous countries looking to add nuclear capacity to lower their carbon emissions from power generation. At the same time, there is a major future supply deficit which will be exacerbated by the Russian situation. There are many small, high-risk players in the sector but we went with PDN as it is relatively low risk with its restart of the Langer Heinrich mine in Namibia.
